header:
Date: 2028-01-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: enabled
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood, AE); Priya Shah (Redwood, SE); Marcus Lee (Skycap, CTO); Ana Torres (Skycap, SecOps); Derek Ng (Skycap, Eng Mgmt); Sofia Ruiz (Skycap, Legal, joined 00:28)
summary: Initial security posture discovery for Skycap Systems evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private deployments. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO attestation, SSO/SAML integration and RBAC, audit log retention and access, customer-managed KMS options (AWS KMS/HSM), data residency (EU regions), and retention/PII handling. Redwood AE/SE outlined deployment options, fallbacks, and next steps to share SOC2 artifacts and schedule technical deep-dive.
topics: SSO / SAML / SCIM and RBAC mapping
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Data residency and retention policy alignment
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'll kick us off - Alex from Redwood, AE, joined by Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marcus Lee: Hi Alex, good - Marcus here. We wanted to get into security and hosting options, basically whether we can use hosted or we need dedicated or full private.
[00:12] Alex Morgan: Great. High level, we'll run through SOC2/ISO, SSO and RBAC, audit logging, encryption/KMS, and then figure next steps. Priya will jump into some of the technical tradeoffs.
[00:22] Priya Shah: Hey all - quick note, I'm going to call out some latency/cost tradeoffs when we talk dedicated vs hosted — also where private makes sense for data residency and air-gapped regs.
[00:31] Ana Torres: Cool. We're SecOps so our checklist is pretty standard: SOC2 or ISO attestation, SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning, fine-grained RBAC, audit logs retention and immutable exports, and we need to know about customer-managed keys. Also EU data residency.
[00:44] Derek Ng: From infra, we also care about network path — VPC peering or private link, and whether KV cache or cache sharing leaks anything.
[00:52] Alex Morgan: Totally. Quick Q: do you have SOC2 Type II today?
[00:55] Marcus Lee: We do internally, but we need our vendors to be SOC2. What do you have?
[00:58] Alex Morgan: Redwood is SOC2 Type II and we have an ISO27001 attestation as well. I'll send the report after the call. There's also a short whitepaper on our KMS integrations and private deployment checklist.
[01:07] Marcus Lee: Great. Can you confirm scope? Like is it only hosted or does it cover Dedicated/Private?
[01:12] Priya Shah: Our SOC2 covers the control plane and hosted API operations. For Dedicated we provide a similar control baseline but the contract shows segregation and SLAs. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, we ship a private control plane and the audit scope differs — we provide artifacts and runbooks — but the customer's ops will own certain controls.
[01:30] Ana Torres: So for private deployments, does Redwood support HSM-backed keys? We cannot have cloud-managed keys for some data.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Yes, we support BYOK with AWS KMS and HSM options. For private/on-prem, you can bring HSMs. For Hosted, we support customer-managed KMS with key usage logs exported to your KMS. 
[01:50] Derek Ng: Does that mean Redwood ever has access to plaintext? Our security team is paranoid about that.
[01:55] Alex Morgan: Short answer: operationally we need to process model inputs/outputs in memory but we don't persist keys; with BYOK we can't decrypt without key grants. We have a notes doc that explains key wrapping and envelope encryption flow.
[02:08] Marcus Lee: Okay. On SSO — we use Okta and have SCIM. How mature is your SAML and SCIM support for automating RBAC?
[02:15] Priya Shah: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with teams and token scoping. You can map SAML attributes to roles and use SCIM for group sync. There are some UI defaults we can turn off for stricter enforcement.
[02:28] Ana Torres: Is there an audit trail that ties actions back to the SAML user id? We need to show who performed model-promote, model-deploy, or data export.
[02:36] Alex Morgan: Yes, audit logs capture user-id, action, resource, timestamp, and request id. Logs are queryable in the Console and exportable via S3 or SIEM connector. Retention defaults to 90 days in hosted; dedicated can configure longer retention and we can ship logs to your S3 for indefinite retention.
[02:53] Derek Ng: Exportable in near-real time or batched daily?
[02:57] Priya Shah: We offer both. Streaming (near-realtime) via Kinesis/Firehose or daily deliveries to S3. For compliance teams we usually do streaming into their SIEM.
[03:06] Marcus Lee: For legal and e-discovery, we need immutable logs for 1 year. Is that supported?
[03:11] Alex Morgan: Hosted default 90 days, but for enterprise customers we can extend retention in Dedicated and Private; we can also provide immutable exports to your storage to meet one-year retention.
[03:20] Ana Torres: About data residency — we need all inference requests for EU customers to be processed in EU region, not just stored there. Does Redwood route by region?
[03:28] Priya Shah: Yes, routing policies allow region pinning. Hosted has EU regions we can pin traffic to. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region or Private VPC installed in your EU cloud.
[03:38] Marcus Lee: How does fallback work? If an EU region is overloaded, will requests fail over to US? 
[03:43] Alex Morgan: Our default is to fail closed for region-pin policies — we won't route out of-region unless you enable a fallback policy. We can configure canary fallbacks for critical apps.
[03:51] Derek Ng: Performance question — Dedicated vs Hosted: what's the typical p95 latency difference?
[03:56] Priya Shah: It depends on model and sequence lengths. Typically dedicated reduces p95 by 10-30% because of pinned capacity and dedicated GPUs; hosted is multi-tenant optimized so sometimes near identical for small models. We'll need your traffic profile to give a precise number.
[04:10] Marcus Lee: We'll share that. For the private deployment, we need a strict change control. Can Redwood integrate with our ticketing for deployments?
[04:18] Alex Morgan: Yes, we integrate with Jira/ServiceNow for deployment approvals and can require CI/CD gating.
[04:23] Ana Torres: On RBAC: do you support attribute-based access control or just role-based? We have use-cases where teams can't access certain models because of data sensitivity.
[04:31] Priya Shah: Primarily role-based with team-scoped policies, but we also have resource tags and policy rules you can use to restrict access. ABAC is on the roadmap, we can share the product timeline.
[04:41] Derek Ng: About audit logs, any PII redaction? Our logs sometimes contain prompts with customer PII.
[04:48] Priya Shah: We can mask or redact prompt content at capture time and also filter PII via scrubbing hooks. For hosted customers, we provide options to disable transcript retention entirely and only keep metadata.
[04:59] Marcus Lee: That's important. Also retention of customer data — what is default?
[05:03] Alex Morgan: Default for hosted is ephemeral inference cache and logs retention 90 days; input and output forwarding to storage only if you enable logging. For Dedicated and Private you can elect to not persist prompts at all.
[05:17] Ana Torres: About certifications — you said ISO 27001 too? Do you have scope docs for that?
[05:22] Alex Morgan: Yes ISO27001 is in-scope for our platform controls; we'll include the scope summary in the package I send.
[05:29] Sofia Ruiz: (joined) Sorry I'm late - quick legal question: for Private on-prem deployment, what indemnity or liability changes?
[05:36] Alex Morgan: Good q — contracts differ for Private and Dedicated. Our legal team can provide the template; it's typical enterprise carve-outs for customer-managed components. I'll loop in legal after this call.
[05:47] Marcus Lee: Any red flags on data exfil? I want to be sure the model provider can't export our datasets.
[05:52] Priya Shah: We have egress controls, VPC restrictions, and no free-floating export endpoints. For hosted, outbound network is restricted and we can provide allow-lists. For private, you're in control.
[06:03] Derek Ng: For billing, does hosted charge per-token only? How about dedicated reserve?
[06:08] Alex Morgan: Hosted is usage-based (per token/per embedding). Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits and lower unit costs; Private is licensed deployments plus support. We'll share pricing tiers.
[06:19] Marcus Lee: Competitors — we evaluated another provider but they didn't offer BYOK with HSM for hosted. Is that unique?
[06:25] Alex Morgan: Not unique but our BYOK and private patterns are mature; we also offer fallbacks and transparent perf benchmarking.
[06:33] Ana Torres: Can you describe the KMS flow quickly? You mentioned envelope encryption.
[06:38] Priya Shah: Sure — we use envelope encryption: customer key in KMS wraps data keys used to encrypt payloads. Data keys are ephemeral in memory. For secrets at rest we use AES-GCM with keys stored via KMS key IDs. For HSM, the key material never leaves the module. Note: audio transcription sometimes calls this K-V catch, sorry that's a transcription artefact.
[06:58] Marcus Lee: If we use BYOK, can we rotate keys and will that invalidate historical logs?
[07:03] Priya Shah: Rotation is supported; old objects remain decryptable if re-encrypted during rotation window. We have a rotation policy doc we'll share.
[07:12] Derek Ng: For audit logging and SIEM ingest, what's the schema? Is user-id the SAML unique id or email?
[07:18] Alex Morgan: It captures both SAML subject and email; we can customize the mapping.
[07:24] Marcus Lee: We need proof that log integrity is preserved. Do you support append-only logs or signed log bundles?
[07:31] Priya Shah: We have tamper-evidence via signed log bundles and can deliver via write-once storage if you request. For enterprise customers we recommend pushing to their WORM-enabled S3 buckets.
[07:43] Ana Torres: For disaster recovery and exposure, how are backups secured?
[07:47] Alex Morgan: Backups of control-data are encrypted at rest and in transit, keys are managed per customer if BYOK is enabled. Backups have restricted access and audit controls.
[07:58] Marcus Lee: Ok. Next, regulatory: we're subject to DP regulations in EU and transfer restrictions. Is there a standard DPA and can you sign EU SCCs?
[08:07] Alex Morgan: We have a DPA and support SCCs in our enterprise contracts; we can include data processing addenda for EU transfers. Legal will follow up.
[08:17] Sofia Ruiz: We'll need to review the DPA and security questionnaires — can you provide the latest security questionnaire answers?
[08:22] Alex Morgan: Yes, we'll send the completed security questionnaire and the SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[08:26] Derek Ng: Anything about model provenance — do you allow customers to pin model versions? We sometimes need to freeze model weights.
[08:33] Priya Shah: Yes, model pinning, versioning, and rollout policies are supported. You can pin to specific variants, including quantized variants. That helps with reproducibility.
[08:42] Marcus Lee: On cost transparency: can we get token-level breakdown and per-route usage?
[08:47] Alex Morgan: Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns and per-model, per-route dashboards. We can grant view-only to finance.
[08:56] Ana Torres: For private deployment, what minimal infra do we need? GPUs, networking, OS versions?
[09:02] Priya Shah: We'll send a deployment checklist — typically a fleet of GPUs (we support A100, H100), Kubernetes 1.27+ recommendations or a lightweight runtime for air-gapped. We'll include sizing charts based on throughput.
[09:15] Marcus Lee: Do you offer a proof-of-concept with limited traffic?
[09:18] Alex Morgan: Yes, we do POCs — often 4-6 weeks with sandboxed dedicated capacity and baseline benchmarks.
[09:24] Derek Ng: For telemetry, do you collect performance traces that include prompt text?
[09:29] Priya Shah: Traces include identifiers and durations; prompt text is optional and can be disabled — we recommend disabling for sensitive workloads.
[09:36] Marcus Lee: We have a few security redlines: no persistent prompt retention in hosted unless explicitly agreed, customer-controlled keys, EU-only processing for EU tenants, and exportable immutable logs. Can Redwood meet these?
[09:48] Alex Morgan: Yes to all, with varying delivery methods: hosted with enterprise config, dedicated with contract terms, or private for strictest control. We'll document specifics.
[09:57] Ana Torres: How about penetration testing? Can we run a vendor-led pen test against a dedicated deployment?
[10:03] Priya Shah: Yes — we coordinate and provide a scope; for hosted there are standard rules, for dedicated/private we can run with you.
[10:11] Marcus Lee: Great. Would like to see an example infra diagram for a private install.
[10:16] Alex Morgan: We'll attach the private deployment architecture and config guide.
[10:20] (longer silence as people review shared link)
[10:48] Marcus Lee: One more question — if we go with hosted initially and later migrate to dedicated or private, how disruptive is the migration?
[10:55] Priya Shah: We've done several migrations. Application-level changes are minimal if you use the same API; data exports and key rotations need planning. We provide a migration runbook and can do a phased cutover.
[11:06] Derek Ng: Do you have a checklist for SOC2 auditors when reviewing Redwood as a vendor?
[11:11] Alex Morgan: Yes, we have an auditor pack with control mappings, evidence, and contact points. We'll send it.
[11:16] Marcus Lee: OK that sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[11:20] Alex Morgan: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, security questionnaire, private deployment diagram, KMS rotation and key flow docs, and pricing tiers. Priya will schedule the technical deep-dive and Derek will share traffic profiles.
[11:33] Sofia Ruiz: Legal will expect the DPA and SCCs; please include redlines early.
[11:37] Alex Morgan: Noted — legal will be included. Any final quick q's?
[11:42] Ana Torres: No, I think we're good. We'll review the docs.
[11:45] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.
[11:46] Alex Morgan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the package by Friday.
[11:50] (call ends)
notes: References shared: /links/redwood-soc2-2027.pdf, /links/private-deploy-arch-2028.pdf, security-questionnaire.xlsx. Customer emphasized EU residency and BYOK HSM requirement; requested signed DPA and SCCs. Priya to run perf benchmarks in follow-up.
